heading.en: ① From the chōza (long-seated) posture: yoko-ukemi with the arm only

prose.en: From the chōza posture, raise both arms and both legs upward as in ushiro-ukemi (rear breakfall), fall diagonally backward, and take the breakfall with one arm. The opposite hand touches the belt; take the breakfall with the left and right arms alternately.

heading.en: ② From the face-up posture: yoko-ukemi using arm and legs

prose.en: From the face-up posture, raise both arms and both legs, turn the body to the side, and strike the tatami hard and simultaneously with both legs and the whole of one arm. Do this alternately to left and right. At this time the lower leg should be forward and the upper leg to the rear.
When tori throws correctly, uke ends up in the yoko-ukemi posture. From the elementary stage it is important to practise repeatedly in pairs, linking the breakfall to the throwing action.

heading.en: ③ From the sonkyo (deep crouch) / chūgoshi (half-crouch) posture

prose.en: From the sonkyo posture, extend one leg diagonally forward, then fall diagonally backward and take the yoko-ukemi (side breakfall).
From the standing posture, extend one leg forward and bend the knee, drop the buttocks close to the heel, and take the yoko-ukemi.

When a technique is actually applied to the right leg, the breakfall has to be taken with the left hand. The reversed breakfall must be practised at the same time. From the sonkyo (or standing) posture, extend one leg forward and bend the knee, drop the buttocks close to the heel, turn the body over and take the yoko-ukemi with the opposite arm.
Practise the reversed breakfall as well.

　①　長座の姿勢から　腕だけの横受け身

第４章　技能指導の要点
　③　そんきょ （中腰）の姿勢から
　そんきょの姿勢から、片方の脚を斜め前方に伸ばした後、斜め後方へ倒れて横受け身をとります。
　④　立位の姿勢から
　立位の姿勢から、片方の脚を前方へ伸ばし膝を曲げ、踵近くに臀部を落とし横受け身をとります。
　⑤　反転した横受け身
　そんきょ（立位）姿勢から、片方の脚を前方へ
伸ばし膝を曲げ、踵の近くに臀部を落とし、体を
反転させ、反対の腕で横受け身をとります。
　⑥　移動しながら
　　ア　継ぎ足で横に移動しながら横受け身
　　イ　歩み足で前方に移動しながら横受け身
